abstract_sentences.text: This paper studies the use of kernel density estimation (KDE) for linear algebraic tasks involving the kernel matrix of a collection of n data points in Rd.

evidence.anchor: This paper studies the use of kernel density estimation (KDE)

abstract_sentences.text: In particular, we improve upon the best existing algorithms for computing the following up to (1 + ε) relative error for a Gaussian kernel matrix and other kernels: matrix-vector products, matrix-matrix products, the spectral norm, and sum of all entries.

evidence.anchor: we improve upon the best existing algorithms

abstract_sentences.text: The runtimes of our algorithms depend linearly on the dimension d, sub-quadratically in the number of points n, and polynomially on the target error ε.

evidence.anchor: depend linearly on the dimension d, sub-quadratically in n

abstract_sentences.text: Importantly, the dependence on n in each case is far lower when accessing the kernel matrix through KDE queries as opposed to reading individual entries.

evidence.anchor: through KDE queries as opposed to reading individual entries

abstract_sentences.text: Our improvements over existing best algorithms (particularly those of [BIMW21] (ICML ‘21)) for these tasks reduce the polynomial dependence on ε, and additionally decrease the dependence on n in the case of computing the sum of all entries.

evidence.anchor: particularly those of [BIMW21]

abstract_sentences.text: For example, we reduce the power of 1/ε from ≈ 7.7 to ≈ 3.2 for a 1 − ε relative error estimation of the spectral norm of a Gaussian kernel matrix.

evidence.anchor: reduce the power of 1/ε from ≈ 7.7 to ≈ 3.2

abstract_sentences.text: We complement our upper bounds with several lower bounds for related problems, which provide (conditional) quadratic time hardness results and additionally hint at the limits of KDE based approaches for the problems we study.

evidence.anchor: (conditional) quadratic time hardness results

final_judgment.single_storyline: Use KDE-query access as a reusable kernel-matrix oracle, redesign the error/sampling interface for downstream linear algebra, then delimit the oracle model with conditional and natural-limit arguments. [p.1-2 Abstract/Introduction; p.8-12 §4; p.30-38 §§9-11]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The front body keeps the task list, prior-best table comparison, theorem statements, query-access rationale, and high-level mechanisms. [p.2-12]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The integrated appendix-style material carries full proofs, parameter balances, OV constructions, implementation detail, and most empirical graphics. It is about 2.3 times the estimated front-body prose. [p.8; p.13-47]
final_judgment.best_pattern: Use a compact task-by-runtime-by-prior table, then repeat prior bottleneck -> mechanism -> theorem -> boundary, with algorithms as concrete handoffs. [p.3-4; p.8-12; p.16, p.20, p.26]
final_judgment.largest_gap: There is no standalone conclusion or limitations synthesis; the mixed-sign original MVP question remains open, the KDE natural limits are not universal lower bounds, and experiments cover only Algorithm 2 in a narrow implementation setting. [p.12; p.18-19; p.30-31; p.33; p.38-45]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When a theoretical performance gain comes from an interchangeable oracle, state the oracle interface and its error propagation independently before attaching downstream tasks. [p.2; p.13-16; p.19-21]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule needs an error direction/scale that downstream proofs can use. Here top-eigenpair analysis depends on non-negative error and the non-negative top eigenvector, so mixed-sign variants do not inherit it automatically. [p.20; p.23-24]

evidence_coverage.coverage_definition: Count of evidence-bearing extracted records in the named deep-read inventories. Each includes at least one PDF physical-page anchor.
